title: Anthropic CEO Calls for Limits on Frontier AI Progress
summary: Dario Amodei argues that frontier AI development needs enforceable speed limits as autonomous research and control risks accelerate.
body:
## What happened

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a policy essay arguing that frontier AI development should be deliberately slowed before model capabilities begin improving faster than institutions can monitor them. His proposal focuses on systems that can conduct autonomous research, improve their own capabilities, or materially increase cybersecurity and biological risks.

Amodei’s argument is broader than a request for voluntary restraint. He calls for mandatory testing and auditing of frontier models above a defined compute threshold, with release blocked or reversed when systems fail safety requirements. He compares the proposed framework with aviation and pharmaceuticals, where technically powerful products are not treated as ordinary software releases.

The essay also calls for international coordination, tighter protection of advanced chips and data-center capacity, and public support for workers affected by rapid automation. Anthropic is positioning these ideas as a practical policy framework rather than a general warning about long-term AI risk.

## Why it matters

The significance lies in the source as much as the proposal. Amodei leads one of the companies competing directly at the frontier, so the essay is both a safety intervention and a statement about how Anthropic wants the next phase of competition governed. It also exposes a growing tension inside the industry: labs want faster capability gains, yet some executives now argue that deployment speed itself should become a regulated variable.

The proposal leaves difficult questions unanswered, including who sets the capability threshold, how tests remain credible when labs control access to models, and whether non-Western developers would accept a shared regime. Still, it moves the debate from broad principles toward concrete controls on training scale, release timing, and autonomous improvement.
title_zh: Anthropic掌门人呼吁为前沿AI设“限速器”
summary_zh: Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊认为，前沿模型必须接受强制测试与审计，以免自主研发速度超出人类控制能力。
body_zh:
## 发生了什么

Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊发表政策文章，主张在模型能力增长速度超过监管和安全评估能力之前，主动放慢前沿人工智能的发展。他重点关注能够自主开展研究、提升自身能力，或显著放大网络安全和生物安全风险的系统。

这并不是一次简单的企业自律倡议。阿莫代伊提出，超过特定算力门槛的前沿模型应接受强制性的第三方测试和审计；如果系统未达到安全要求，监管机构应阻止其发布，甚至要求撤回。他把人工智能与航空器、药品相提并论，认为高风险模型不应被当作普通软件直接上线。

文章还呼吁各国协调监管标准，收紧先进芯片和数据中心能力的扩散，并通过公共政策帮助应对快速自动化带来的就业冲击。Anthropic试图把这套主张包装成一份可执行的政策框架，而不仅是对长期风险的泛泛提醒。

## 为什么重要

这篇文章的分量，既来自内容，也来自作者身份。阿莫代伊正领导一家直接参与前沿竞争的模型公司，因此这既是一份安全政策主张，也是在为Anthropic希望看到的下一阶段竞争规则定调。行业内部的矛盾正在变得清晰：实验室希望更快提升能力，但部分掌门人已经开始主张把发布速度本身纳入监管。

方案仍留下许多关键问题：能力门槛由谁制定，模型由企业控制时第三方测试如何保持可信，非西方开发者是否会接受统一制度。不过，它确实把讨论从原则口号推进到训练规模、发布时间和自主改进能力等更具体的控制点。

sources.title: Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AI

featured_reason: It is the clearest fresh attempt by a frontier-model leader to turn AI safety concerns into concrete controls on development speed.
featured_reason_zh: 这是本期最明确的一次前沿模型公司掌门人行动：把AI安全担忧转化为对研发速度和发布机制的具体约束。
cat_take_zh: 阿莫代伊把“放慢”具体化为算力门槛、审计和撤回机制，真正难点是跨国执行。
cat_take_en: Amodei makes “slowing down” operational through compute thresholds and audits; enforcement across borders remains the hard part.
